We anticipate increased cost from our third-party service providers beginning in the second half of fiscal year 2027, or the first half of calendar year 2027, as providers seek to offset heightened expenses resulting, in part, from budget pressures associated with the Reconciliation Act, budget cuts to providers from state Medicaid programs, as well as possible increases in other costs in order to provide…
We did not experience a material increase to our cost of care and external provider costs during the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 and do not anticipate a material increase in the second quarter.

We continue to believe that our ongoing clinical and operational value initiatives may assist us in reducing unnecessary utilization and offsetting the increased costs anticipated in the later part of fiscal year 2027.
In Colorado, where we serve the largest cohort of our PACE census, we anticipate a decrease in Medicaid premium rates,
We also expect to face Medicaid reimbursement wage pressures from other states that release rates effective January 1, 2027, such as California, which could impact the latter half of our fiscal year.

As a result, while we have not experienced any material impacts during the first quarter, we continue to expect the rate pressures to impact the Company's margins in fiscal 2027 and continue to monitor the full effects of the Reconciliation Act on the Company.

As we serve more participants in existing centers, we expect to leverage our fixed cost base at those centers and increase the value of a center to our business over time.

We also have pursued and intend to continue pursuing additional relationships with key stakeholders, existing organizations and other care providers in order to form partnerships in target geographies.
We intend to continue investing in our centers, value-based care model, and sales and marketing initiatives to support long-term growth.
We expect our expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the foreseeable future to support our growth and as the result of current and potential legal and regulatory proceedings.
We plan to continue investing in our growth while also maintaining focus on managing our results of operations.

While many of the anticipated benefits are expected to be realized over time, we believe certain benefits from these investment are beginning to emerge, and we expect these investments to positively impact our business and results of operations over the longer term.
When we open new centers, we expect cost of care, excluding depreciation and amortization, to increase in absolute dollars due to higher census and facility related costs.
We expect these costs to increase in absolute dollars over time as we continue to grow our participant census.

However, over the long term, we anticipate corporate, general and administrative expenses to decrease as a percentage of revenue as we gain operating leverage, although such expenses may fluctuate as a percentage of revenue from period to period due to the timing and amount of these expenses.
